In summary, our research is concerned with
the morphological demonstration of a non‐disordered megakaryopoietic process which may be responsible for the development of a thrombocytosis in CML.

the demonstration of the existence of an increased number of megakaryoblastic cells in the marrow of CML patients, particularly in cases of thrombocytosis, and with the evidence of a disorderly expansion of megakaryocytosis, which is characterized by a significant increase in the total number of megakryocytes and by the presence of small and immature megakaryocellular elements.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in CML a non‐disordered expansion of megakaryocytosis takes place, but with the appearance of a distinct megakaryocentric dysplasia, particularly in patients with an elevated platelet count.
, in contrast to the classical concept of CML, a disorderly expansion of megakaryocytosis in CML can be detected by morphometric and morphological analysis.
in CML a non‐disordered megakaryopoietic process with a significant increase in megakaryocytes is present, but with a tendency to smaller cell sizes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in CML, in contrast to acute megakaryoblastic leukemia (AMKL) a non‐disordered megakaryopoietic proliferation with a relative increase of the megakarocytic precursor cell pool occurs, which may lead to thrombocythema.
in CML, the megakaryocytosis is characterized by an expansion of the precursor pool and by the development of small megakaryocytes.
in CML a non‐disordered megakaryocytosis is detectable which may be related to the thrombocytosis in the majority of the patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the morphometric analysis of the bone marrow trephine biopsy in CML is a useful tool for the detection of an abnormal megakaryopoietic process.

the morphometric analysis of bone marrow tissue from CML patients by means of the monoclonal antibody Y2/51 is a valuable tool for a better understanding of the megakariocytic proliferation in CML and for the identification of patients with a high risk of transformation.
a quantitative assessment of megakaryocytopoiesis in CML is feasible and can provide additional information on the biological behaviour of this disorder.
